about: Adversarial KT matrix. Written 18 Oct before any output was seen. Each case is a short transcript run through the real pipeline (no LLM) by evaluation/matrix.py. Checks: shows / shows_any (normalised text visible somewhere in the document), absent / absent_re (not visible outside conflict warnings), never_alone (every document unit naming `text` also names `with`, so a superseded or hedged value is never shown on its own), verbatim (exact characters), in_section, order (same section, in order), flagged (shown in a conflict or gap warning), not_flagged (no conflict warning names both), coverage, completes. level: must = a wrong final document; should = a desirable behaviour the product does not promise yet.

cases.title: Question-and-answer handover with a speaker label on every turn
transcript: Priya: Can you walk me through Tern before you leave?
Sam: Sure. Tern is the parcel label service for our warehouses.
Priya: How do I deploy it?
Sam: Merge to main and Azure DevOps deploys to the staging slot. Check the smoke tests, then swap the slot into production. If it goes wrong, swap back.
Priya: What breaks most often?
Sam: The printer queue backs up when a warehouse goes offline. Clear the queue from the admin page, and if that doesn't help, call the warehouse IT team.
Priya: How many labels a day?
Sam: About twelve thousand a day.
Priya: Who owns it?
Sam: The logistics platform team owns Tern.

expect.text: Clear the queue from the admin page

expect.pattern: common failures & fixes.*not discussed:[^|]*fixes or workarounds
\b(how do i deploy it|what breaks most often|who owns it|how many labels a day)\?
